newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BMW, Chrysler team up to build Brazil motor plant.
newsitem.headline: BMW, Chrysler team up to build Brazil motor plant.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) said Monday it has teamed up with Chrysler Corp. to build a $500 million motor plant in Brazil by 1999 and also plans to build a $150 million Land Rover assembly plant.
The projects are the latest in a wave of planned auto investments in Brazil as global automakers jostle to gain a foothold in one of the world's fast-growing car markets.
"BMW group and Chrysler have decided to build an engine factory together, and this plant will definitely be in Brazil," Michael Turwitt, BMW do Brasil Ltda president, said at a news conference.
"BMW group intends to build a car factory here as well," he said.

Renault SA, Daimler-Benz AG unit Mercedes-Benz, Honda Motor Co. Ltd., Toyota Motor Corp. and Asia Motors Co. Ltd. have each unveiled their first Brazil projects while four others already operating in Brazil -- Volkswagen AG, Fiat SpA, General Motors Corp. and Ford Motor Co. -- announced expansions in the country, all in the past year.
BMW AG's local unit plans to assemble up to 15,000 Land Rover Defenders at its new Brazil plant by 1998, Turwitt added. Rover is a subsidiary of BMW.
Part of the plant's output will be exported to Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina, Brazil's partners in the Mercosur economic alliance.
BMW and Chrysler each will invest $250 million in an engine plant to produce 400,000 engines a year in a project that will create 3,000 jobs, directly and indirectly.

The plant will produce late-model 1.4-litre and 1.6-litre engines, which will be exported to Asia and Europe and also be used in the production of Chrysler compact vehicles and BMW's Rover cars, Turwitt said.
The companies have not decided yet where the plants will be built but they will be in Brazil's southern or southeastern regions, he said.
"We expect to announce locations for the plants in the first quarter this year," Turwitt said.
BMW also plans to import Rover 200s and other vehicles from the Rover family to Brazil, he said.
